title: Rabbi Yaakov bar Abaye
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in the Yerushalmi: [Berakhot ch. 2, end of halakha 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.2.3.19) (פ״ב סה״ג); [Moed Katan ch. 3, halakha 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Moed_Katan.3.1.12); [Sanhedrin ch. 10, halakha 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.10.2.6), where he speaks in the name of Rabbi Acha; and in [Megillah ch. 1, halakha 9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.1.9.8) and in [Ruth Rabbah at the end of ch. 8](https://www.sefaria.org/Ruth_Rabbah.8.1), the reading is 'bar Abbaiah'; and in [Moed Katan ch. 3, halakha 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Moed_Katan.3.1.12) and [Sukkah ch. 1, halakha 6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sukkah.1.6.3) he speaks in the name of Rav Sheshet.[^2]

The Introduction to the Yerushalmi suggests that he was the son of Abaye, Rava’s colleague. It cites [Yoma 27a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.27a.1), where Abaye explains a teaching to his son. On this view, the son went from Babylonia to the Land of Israel in his youth, which would explain his absence from the Bavli. But it is very difficult to say this, because in the days of Abaye the decrees in the Land of Israel were so numerous that almost the majority of the sages of the Land of Israel went down to Babylonia with Ravin, as is explained in his entry.[^1]

And in [Bamidbar Rabbah 2:26](https://www.sefaria.org/Bamidbar_Rabbah.2.26), Rabbi Yaakov bar Ivo is cited in the name of Rabbi Acha, and it should read 'bar Abaye', as in Tanchuma Acharei [par.] 19; and it is very close to say that he is Rabbi Yaakov bar Abaye of Bardelia who is mentioned in [Sheviit ch. 2, halakha 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sheviit.2.4.4).

notes.text: Yoma describes Abaye explaining a teaching to his son without naming him. The introduction to the Yerushalmi proposes that he was this Yaakov. Hyman finds that identification very difficult on chronological grounds.

The linked Yerushalmi passages and Ruth Rabbah preserve Abaye and Abbaiah forms. The Sukkah passage includes Rav Sheshet and Rabbi Chiyya Rabbah in its chain. The Ruth Rabbah passage is 8:1 in the linked edition. Bamidbar Rabbah has Yaakov bar Ivo, and Sheviit names Yaakov bar Abaye of Bardelia.
